The churches behaved inconsistently. The German Christians wanted to merge Protestantism with National Socialism, against which the Confessing Church took a stand in 1934 with the Barmen Declaration; pastors such as Martin Niemöller and Dietrich Bonhoeffer ended up in concentration camps for it. In 1933 the Catholic Church concluded a concordat with Hitler, yet the sermons of the Münster bishop Clemens August von Galen against the killing of the sick and disabled forced the regime in 1941 to conceal and relocate the murders of Aktion T4. A united resistance of the churches against the Holocaust did not materialize; individuals such as the Berlin cathedral provost Bernhard Lichtenberg paid for their public prayer for the Jews with their lives.

The war accelerated science as never before. Otto Hahn and Lise Meitner had discovered nuclear fission in 1938; in the United States the Manhattan Project under Robert Oppenheimer built the atomic bomb from it by 1945. Radar, the British computing system Colossus and Konrad Zuse's Z3 of 1941 laid the foundations of the computer age, the mass production of penicillin saved countless wounded, and the German V2 rocket was built by concentration camp prisoners in the tunnels of Mittelbau-Dora, where more people died than were killed by the weapon itself. Doctors of the regime carried out human experiments in concentration camps that were tried after the war in the Nuremberg Doctors' Trial and led to the Nuremberg Code on the consent of test subjects.
zweiter-weltkrieg#sections.3.title: Economy and Technology
The National Socialists overcame unemployment with motorway construction, job creation and above all a gigantic rearmament that was financed through concealed credit and brought the state to the brink of bankruptcy in 1939. The Four-Year Plan of 1936 under Göring was meant to make Germany capable of war within four years and drove forward the production of synthetic gasoline and rubber. The expropriation of the Jews, euphemistically called Aryanization, brought the state and German businessmen assets worth billions. During the war the Reich plundered the occupied countries: France paid occupation costs, and under the Hunger Plan Ukraine was to supply grain while millions of people were to starve.

From 1942, armaments minister Albert Speer increased German weapons production threefold by 1944 despite the bombing, relying on forced laborers and concentration camp prisoners requisitioned by corporations such as IG Farben, Krupp and Siemens. Yet against the combined economic power of the Allies, Germany had no chance: even before entering the war, the United States supplied weapons and trucks to Great Britain and the Soviet Union under the Lend-Lease Act of 1941, built Liberty ships in days instead of months and produced almost 300,000 aircraft by 1945. Soviet industry in the Urals manufactured the T-34 tank in greater numbers than all German tank works combined.

Technology decided battles. The Battle of the Atlantic, in which German submarines sought to cut off Great Britain's supplies, was met by the Allies with convoys, radar, direction finders and the decryption of Enigma radio traffic at Bletchley Park. In the Pacific, aircraft carriers replaced battleships as the main weapon, the German Me 262 was the first jet fighter in service in 1944, and the V2 was the first rocket to reach the edge of space. For the period after the war, the Allies planned a new world economic order at Bretton Woods in 1944, with fixed exchange rates, the dollar as the reserve currency, the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#summary: Two superpowers divide the world into blocs, the colonies of Asia and Africa become independent, and from 1989 to 1991 the Eastern bloc and the Soviet Union collapse.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#overview.0: After 1945 the victorious powers of the United States and the Soviet Union soon faced each other as opponents. Europe was divided by the Iron Curtain, Germany was split into two states, and in 1961 the Berlin Wall cemented the separation. Both sides armed themselves with nuclear weapons and waged proxy wars in Korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan. In the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 the world stood on the brink of nuclear war. At the same time the competition between the systems drove science and technology forward, all the way to the Moon landing of 1969.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#overview.1: In parallel, the European colonial empires fell apart. India and Pakistan became independent in 1947, and in the 1950s and 1960s almost all the states of Africa and Asia followed, in part peacefully, in part after bloody wars as in Algeria or Vietnam. In China, Mao Zedong established the People's Republic in 1949, and in the Middle East the State of Israel came into being in 1948, which led to wars with the Arab neighbors and to a conflict with the Palestinians that remains unresolved to this day. The new states of the so-called Third World sought their own path between the blocs.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#overview.2: In Western Europe the Marshall Plan and European integration led to prosperity and democracy; the European Communities of 1957 grew out of the Coal and Steel Community of 1951. The oil crisis of 1973 ended the long economic miracle and revealed the West's dependence on the raw materials of other regions. In the East the planned economy stagnated; attempts at reform such as the Prague Spring of 1968 were crushed. In southern Europe the dictatorships in Portugal, Greece and Spain ended in the 1970s, and in Latin America military regimes succeeded one another until many countries returned to democracy in the 1980s.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#overview.3: After a phase of détente, the antagonism intensified again around 1980. The Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan in 1979, NATO decided to deploy new intermediate-range missiles, and US President Ronald Reagan relied on a massive arms build-up. In Poland the independent trade union Solidarity challenged the communist regime from 1980. Only Mikhail Gorbachev opened the way to change from 1985 with glasnost and perestroika and concluded disarmament treaties with the United States.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#overview.4: In 1989 a peaceful revolution swept away the communist regimes in Eastern Europe; on 9 November the Berlin Wall fell, and on 3 October 1990 Germany was reunified. In China, by contrast, the leadership had the democracy movement on Tiananmen Square bloodily suppressed in June 1989. In July 1991 the Warsaw Pact dissolved, and after a failed coup by conservative communists in August, the Soviet Union broke apart into fifteen independent states in December 1991. This ended the Cold War, which had shaped the world for almost half a century.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#consequences.0: The end of the Cold War ended the division of Europe and of Germany and cleared the way for the democratization of Central and Eastern Europe.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#consequences.1: Decolonization multiplied the number of independent states; the United Nations grew from 51 founding members to more than 160 members in 1991.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#consequences.2: Nuclear weapons, spaceflight, computers and satellites, which arose in the competition between the systems, shape security, the economy and everyday life to this day.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#consequences.3: The struggle against colonialism, racial segregation and apartheid strengthened human rights and civil rights movements worldwide.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#consequences.4: Many conflicts of the present, for instance in the Middle East, in Afghanistan, on the Korean peninsula and over Taiwan, have their roots in the era of the Cold War and decolonization.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#keyFacts.0: In 1948/49 the Western powers supply West Berlin, blockaded by the Soviet Union, by means of the airlift; in 1949 NATO and two German states come into being.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#keyFacts.1: From 1950 to 1953 the Korean War becomes the first hot war of the Cold War; in 1955 the Soviet Union founds the Warsaw Pact as a counterpart to NATO.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#keyFacts.2: In 1960, the so-called Year of Africa, 17 African states become independent; in 1961 the Non-Aligned Movement is founded in Belgrade.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#keyFacts.3: From 1965 to 1973 US troops fight in vain in Vietnam against the communist North, which conquers the South in 1975; in 1968 the Warsaw Pact crushes the Prague Spring.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#keyFacts.4: In 1979 the Soviet Union invades Afghanistan; in 1980 the independent trade union Solidarity is founded in Poland.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#keyFacts.5: In 1986 a reactor explodes at Chernobyl; in June 1989 China's leadership has the protests on Tiananmen Square put down.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#keyFacts.6: On 9 November 1989 the Berlin Wall falls, on 3 October 1990 Germany is reunified, and in December 1991 the Soviet Union dissolves.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#sections.0.title: Rule and Politics
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#sections.0.paragr: The order of the Cold War rested on two alliance systems. With the Truman Doctrine of 1947, the United States committed itself to supporting any government threatened by a communist takeover; this policy of containment found its military form in NATO in 1949. The Soviet Union responded in 1955 with the Warsaw Pact and bound the states of Eastern Europe to itself through communist single parties, secret services and economic treaties. Any country that tried to break out of this bloc, such as Hungary in 1956 or Czechoslovakia in 1968, was brought back with tanks; in 1968 Leonid Brezhnev made the limited sovereignty of the socialist states a doctrine.

Between the blocs, the new states of Asia and Africa sought a third way. At the Bandung Conference of 1955 and in the Non-Aligned Movement from 1961, politicians such as Nehru, Nasser, Sukarno and Tito called for self-determination, disarmament and economic justice. At the same time many of these countries became the scenes of proxy wars in which Washington and Moscow propped up or toppled governments, for example in the Congo, in Angola, Chile or Afghanistan. In the 1970s the policy of détente softened the antagonisms: treaties on the limitation of strategic weapons and the Helsinki Final Act of 1975 created rules that civil rights activists in the East could later invoke.

Around 1980 a new ice age began: after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan many Western states boycotted the Olympic Games in Moscow, and NATO's Double-Track Decision of 1979 led to the deployment of new missiles in Western Europe, against which hundreds of thousands demonstrated. Mikhail Gorbachev, at the head of the Soviet Union from 1985, sought accommodation instead, agreed with Ronald Reagan in 1987 to abolish intermediate-range missiles and refrained from violently suppressing the reform movements in Eastern Europe. After the revolutions of 1989, the Two Plus Four Treaty of 1990 settled the external questions of German unity. In 1991 the Warsaw Pact and the Soviet Union dissolved, and the confrontation of the blocs was over.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#sections.1.title: Society and Everyday Life
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#sections.1.paragr: In Western Europe the economic miracle of the 1950s and 1960s brought full employment and put cars, refrigerators and televisions into millions of households. From 1955 the Federal Republic recruited guest workers from Italy, Greece, Spain and Turkey, out of which an immigration society developed. In the GDR and the Eastern bloc states, the state guaranteed work, housing and childcare, but monitored the lives of its citizens through secret services such as the Stasi and restricted travel and freedom of opinion. The consumer world of the West, visible on West German television, became a silent argument against the system.

The 1960s called the old authorities into question. In the United States the civil rights movement around Rosa Parks and Martin Luther King won the end of legal racial segregation, and in 1968 students in Berkeley, Paris, Berlin and Mexico City protested against the Vietnam War, ossified universities and their parents' generation. The contraceptive pill, the women's movement and new divorce and equality laws changed family life; in Switzerland women received the vote only in 1971. The environmental and peace movements of the 1970s and 1980s, reinforced by Chernobyl, brought green parties into the parliaments.

The world's population grew from 2.5 billion in 1950 to around 5.3 billion in 1990, above all in Asia, Africa and Latin America. Medical progress lowered child mortality, and millions of people moved from the countryside to rapidly growing cities such as Cairo, Mexico City or Calcutta. After independence many new states built schools and universities, so that the share of people who could read and write rose markedly. Migration from the former colonies to Great Britain, France and the Netherlands changed the societies of Western Europe.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#sections.2.title: Culture, Religion and Knowledge
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#sections.2.paragr: Pop culture became the West's export hit: rock 'n' roll, Hollywood films, jeans and Coca-Cola spread an attitude to life that young people followed behind the Iron Curtain as well, while the Eastern bloc states countered with socialist realism and state-sponsored art. From the 1950s onward, television became the leading medium, bringing the Moon landing, the Vietnam War and the fall of the Wall into living rooms. Literature and film dealt with the world war and the Holocaust, dictatorship and exile, from Anne Frank's diary through Alexander Solzhenitsyn's The Gulag Archipelago to Gabriel García Márquez and the Latin American novel.

Science experienced an unprecedented upswing, often financed by the competition between the systems. In 1953 Watson, Crick and Franklin deciphered the structure of DNA, vaccines against polio and the eradication of smallpox in 1980 lengthened life, and the Green Revolution with high-yielding grain varieties averted famines in Asia. The transistor of 1947 and the microchip made computers small and cheap, and in the 1980s the personal computer moved into offices and homes. Out of ARPANET, a research network of the US Department of Defense from 1969, grew the internet, on which the World Wide Web emerged at the end of the epoch.

Religion remained a formative force. The Second Vatican Council from 1962 to 1965 opened the Catholic Church to the modern world, liberation theology in Latin America took the side of the poor, and from 1978 the Polish pope John Paul II strengthened the resistance to communism. The Iranian Revolution of 1979 made political Islam a power, and in the war against the Soviet troops in Afghanistan fighters from many Islamic countries gathered in the 1980s. In Europe, by contrast, the churches lost many members, and society became increasingly secular.
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#sections.3.title: Economy and Technology
kalter-krieg-gegenwart#sections.3.paragr: After 1945 the world economy in the West followed the rules of Bretton Woods: a fixed exchange rate against the dollar, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, and the reduction of tariffs. The Marshall Plan, reconstruction and the social market economy of Ludwig Erhard gave Western Europe three decades of growth, and Japan rose to become the second-largest industrial nation. In the East, planned economies relied on heavy industry and five-year plans; they raised the standard of living at first, but later could not keep up with the consumer goods and computer technology of the West and contributed to the collapse of 1989.

The oil crises of 1973 and 1979 ended the boom, and inflation and unemployment rose. From 1979 Margaret Thatcher in Great Britain and from 1981 Ronald Reagan in the United States responded with privatization, tax cuts and deregulation; the power of the trade unions declined and that of the financial markets grew. At the same time, from 1978 Deng Xiaoping gradually opened China to the market economy and foreign capital, for instance in special economic zones such as Shenzhen. In the 1980s many countries in Latin America and Africa fell into a severe debt crisis that was remembered as the lost decade.

Technology changed everyday life at ever shorter intervals: the jet aircraft and the nuclear power plant in the 1950s, the container ship, the pocket calculator and the color television in the 1960s and 1970s, the personal computer and the first mobile phones in the 1980s. At the same time awareness grew of the limits to growth, as a much-discussed report to the Club of Rome was called in 1972. Acid rain, the ozone hole and reactor accidents such as Chernobyl in 1986 made environmental protection a political task; in 1987 the Montreal Protocol set out the phase-out of ozone-depleting substances, and in 1988 the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change was founded.
gegenwart#summary: After the end of the Cold War, markets, networks and states grow ever closer together, yet terror, wars, financial crises, a pandemic and climate change reveal the vulnerability of the globalized world.
gegenwart#overview.0: With the dissolution of the Soviet Union in December 1991 the Cold War came to an end, and out of the remains of the Eastern bloc emerged fifteen successor states of the USSR as well as new democracies in Central and Eastern Europe. Many observers expected an era of peace in which democracy and the market economy would prevail everywhere. With the Treaty of Maastricht, signed in 1992, the European Community became the European Union in 1993; it introduced the euro in 1999 and admitted ten new members in 2004. At the same time the wars in disintegrating Yugoslavia and the genocide in Rwanda in 1994 showed that nationalism and mass violence had by no means been overcome.
gegenwart#overview.1: Globalization accelerated at an unprecedented pace. Free trade agreements, container ships and the World Wide Web linked markets and people, and countries such as China and India opened up to the world market. With its accession to the World Trade Organization in 2001, China became the workshop of the world and in 2010 rose to become the second-largest economy. Hundreds of millions of people escaped extreme poverty, but in the old industrial regions of the West jobs were lost, and inequality within many countries grew.
gegenwart#overview.2: The attacks of 11 September 2001 ushered in an age of the fight against terror. The United States and its allies waged wars in Afghanistan and Iraq that lasted a long time, claimed many victims and achieved their goals only in part. The Arab Spring of 2011 awakened hopes of democracy in the Middle East, but in Syria, Libya and Yemen it led to civil wars that forced millions of people to flee. The Hamas attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 and the ensuing war in Gaza intensified the Middle East conflict once again.
gegenwart#overview.3: The global financial crisis of 2008 and the COVID-19 pandemic from 2020 made visible how closely the world is interwoven and how quickly crises spread. In many countries populist movements gained support by mobilizing against elites, immigration and international ties; in 2016 the British voted to leave the EU. Russia under Vladimir Putin annexed Crimea in 2014 and on 24 February 2022 launched a full-scale war of aggression against Ukraine, the largest war in Europe since 1945.
gegenwart#overview.4: At the same time technology and science fundamentally changed everyday life. By 2025 the smartphone and social media had connected more than half of humanity via the internet, the decoding of the human genome opened new paths in medicine, and from 2022 artificial intelligence became usable by a broad public. Climate change rose to become the great question facing humanity: with the Paris Agreement of 2015 almost all states committed themselves to limiting global warming. The rivalry between the United States and China shapes a world order in which several powers compete for influence.
gegenwart#consequences.0: By 2013 the European Union had grown to 28 members, created a single market with a common currency for many of its states and became a central political framework for Europe, even though Great Britain left it in 2020.
gegenwart#consequences.1: The rise of China and other emerging economies shifted the world's economic weight toward Asia and ended the dominance of the West in world trade.
gegenwart#consequences.2: The internet, the smartphone and artificial intelligence changed work, education, the public sphere and politics and raise new questions about data protection, disinformation and the power of large technology companies.
gegenwart#consequences.3: Wars from Yugoslavia via Afghanistan, Iraq and Syria to Ukraine and Gaza showed the limits of international peacekeeping and triggered large movements of refugees.
gegenwart#consequences.4: Climate change, pandemics and financial crises made clear that the central problems of the present can be solved only through international cooperation.
gegenwart#keyFacts.0: In February 1992 the Treaty of Maastricht is signed; when it comes into force in 1993 the European Union is born.
gegenwart#keyFacts.1: From 1991 to 1999 Yugoslavia breaks apart in wars; in Srebrenica around 8,000 Bosnian Muslims are murdered in July 1995.
gegenwart#keyFacts.2: In 1994 apartheid ends in South Africa, and in Rwanda around 800,000 people are murdered within about 100 days.
gegenwart#keyFacts.3: On 11 September 2001 al-Qaeda terrorists kill almost 3,000 people in the United States; in December 2001 China joins the World Trade Organization.
gegenwart#keyFacts.4: In 2007 Apple presents the iPhone, in 2008 a global financial crisis shakes the economy, and in 2011 the Arab Spring begins.
gegenwart#keyFacts.5: In 2015 almost all states adopt the Paris Climate Agreement; in 2016 Great Britain votes to leave the EU.
gegenwart#keyFacts.6: From 2020 the COVID-19 pandemic spreads; on 24 February 2022 Russia begins a full-scale war of aggression against Ukraine.
gegenwart#sections.0.title: Rule and Politics
gegenwart#sections.0.paragraphs.0: After the end of the Soviet Union, the United States was the only superpower for about a decade. From 1999 and 2004 respectively, NATO and the European Union admitted many states of Central and Eastern Europe that longed for security and prosperity in the West. In Russia the reforms of Boris Yeltsin led to economic chaos; from 2000 his successor Vladimir Putin built an authoritarian state that controlled the media, the opposition and the judiciary. Moscow increasingly regarded NATO's eastward expansion as a threat and used military force in Georgia in 2008, in Crimea in 2014 and in Ukraine from 2022.
gegenwart#sections.0.paragraphs.1: New forms of international justice emerged: in 1993 and 1994 the United Nations set up criminal tribunals for the former Yugoslavia and for Rwanda, and in 2002 the International Criminal Court in The Hague began its work. At the same time the UN Security Council was often blocked because the veto powers pursued opposing interests, for instance in the Syrian war. After 2001 the United States waged wars in Afghanistan and Iraq that ended without lasting success; in 2021 the Taliban returned to power in Kabul.
gegenwart#sections.0.paragraphs.2: In Africa and Latin America elections and multiparty systems took hold in many places: South Africa became a democracy in 1994, in Brazil, Chile and Mexico elected governments succeeded one another, and in 2002 the African states founded the African Union. Yet military coups, civil wars and authoritarian rulers remained widespread. From the 2010s, populist parties and politicians who turned against immigration, globalization and the established media gained influence in many established democracies. The contrast between democracies and authoritarian states such as China and Russia became a guiding theme of world politics.
gegenwart#sections.1.title: Society and Everyday Life
gegenwart#sections.1.paragraphs.0: The world's population grew from about 5.4 billion in 1991 to over 8 billion in 2022, and since about 2007 the majority of people have lived in cities. Megacities such as Lagos, Dhaka, Shanghai or São Paulo grew rapidly, often with large slums on their outskirts. Life expectancy rose worldwide, child mortality fell markedly, and the share of people in extreme poverty dropped to under one in ten by 2019. In Europe, Japan and China, by contrast, societies aged because fewer children were born.
gegenwart#sections.1.paragraphs.1: Migration shaped the present like hardly any other issue. People left their homes because of wars, persecution and poverty or in search of work; in 2015 more than a million people, many of them from Syria, Afghanistan and Iraq, sought protection in Europe. By 2024, according to the United Nations, more than 120 million people worldwide had fled or been displaced, most of them within their own country or in neighboring states. Immigration societies argued fiercely about integration, borders and asylum.
gegenwart#sections.1.paragraphs.2: In many countries women gained more rights and higher educational qualifications; with Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, Angela Merkel and Jacinda Ardern, women led states and governments. From 2017 the MeToo movement made sexual harassment and violence an issue worldwide. In many states the rights of homosexual people were strengthened; in 2001 the Netherlands became the first country to introduce same-sex marriage. At the same time girls in some regions remained excluded from school, for instance in Afghanistan after the return of the Taliban in 2021.
gegenwart#sections.2.title: Culture, Religion and Knowledge
gegenwart#sections.2.paragraphs.0: The World Wide Web, search engines, the online encyclopedia Wikipedia from 2001 and social networks changed how people find knowledge, inform themselves and talk with one another. With the smartphone, from 2007 billions of people carried a computer with a camera and internet access. Social media made protest movements possible, as in the Arab Spring, but also spread hate speech, conspiracy narratives and targeted disinformation. Streaming services and platforms made music, films and series from South Korea, Nigeria or India known worldwide.
gegenwart#sections.2.paragraphs.1: Science made great progress. In 2003 the Human Genome Project was completed, and new methods such as the CRISPR-Cas9 gene scissors, for which Emmanuelle Charpentier and Jennifer Doudna received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2020, made targeted interventions in the genome possible. During the coronavirus pandemic effective vaccines were developed within a year, including the first mRNA vaccines. Artificial intelligence learned to process language, images and protein structures from vast amounts of data; in 2024 researchers in this field were awarded the Nobel Prizes in Physics and Chemistry.
gegenwart#sections.2.paragraphs.2: Religion remained an important force in world politics. Islamist groups such as al-Qaeda and the so-called Islamic State invoked Islam to justify terror and violence, while the great majority of Muslims rejected this violence. In Africa, Latin America and Asia evangelical and Pentecostal congregations grew rapidly, whereas in Europe the large churches lost many members. Abuse scandals shook the Catholic Church from the 2000s, and in 2013 Francis became the first pope from Latin America.
gegenwart#sections.3.title: Economy and Technology
gegenwart#sections.3.paragraphs.0: After 1991 the market economy prevailed almost worldwide. Free trade agreements such as NAFTA of 1994, the founding of the World Trade Organization in 1995 and the European single market lowered trade barriers, and companies spread their production across continents. India opened up to the world market from 1991, and after joining the WTO in 2001 China became the world's largest exporter. Since 1999 many EU states have shared the euro as a common currency.
gegenwart#sections.3.paragraphs.1: Globalization also brought severe crises. The Asian financial crisis of 1997, the bursting of the dot-com bubble in 2000 and above all the global financial crisis of 2008, triggered by bad mortgage loans in the United States, plunged many countries into recession. In the euro crisis from 2010, states such as Greece had to be propped up with loans worth billions. In 2020 the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted supply chains, paralyzed entire industries and led to high public debt and later to rising inflation.
gegenwart#sections.3.paragraphs.2: Technology developed rapidly: mobile phones, broadband internet, smartphones, cloud services and artificial intelligence followed one another in quick succession. A few technology companies from the United States and China rose to become the most valuable companies in the world. Greenhouse gas emissions reached record levels, and global warming led to more heat waves, droughts and floods. In many countries wind and solar energy became the cheapest form of electricity generation, and electric cars spread, above all in China and Europe.
